title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: EV motorcycle adoption plans
sections.summary: The passage asks about the Ministry's plans to roll out affordable EV motorcycles and needed infrastructure, and whether there is an updated assessment of early adoption incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We have already taken steps to enhance the charging infrastructure for increased adoption of electric vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These are important steps, but what are the Ministry's plans to roll out affordable EV motorcycles, for example, and the infrastructure needed for that as part of its sustainability efforts in our land transport plans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is there an updated assessment of possible early adoption incentives for EV motorcycles.

sections.label: Transport sustainability targets and strategies
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Government's sustainability targets are across land, air and sea transportation and what the Ministry's strategies are to achieve them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Bearing in mind that other countries are not sitting on their laurels and are always looking at chipping away our rankings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask, what are the Government's sustainability targets across land, air and sea transportation and what are the Ministry's strategies to achieve these targets?

sections.label: EV charging infrastructure costs
sections.summary: The passage asks about expected annual expenditure for installing and maintaining EV charging infrastructure and substations, and whether charging fees will recover development expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Working backwards from the 2040 target for 100% cleaner EVs, what is the expected annual expenditure required for installing and maintaining EV charging infrastructure and the cost of additional substations needed to meet the higher power load?

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Are there plans to recover part of the development expenses required for EV charging infrastructure from charging fees levied on drivers of EV cars?

sections.label: AAFC fixed at $700
sections.summary: The passage states the AAFC is fixed from this year at $700 per year and that MOT said it sought to put EV users on par with ICE vehicle users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The AAFC is fixed from this year as $700 per year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Parliamentary answer to Sengkang Member of Parliament Mr Louis Chua in May 2021, MOT stated that the AAFC sought to put EV users on par with those using internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As ICE vehicle users paid fuel excise duties at the pump, but EV users did not, AAFC was added to put both categories of vehicle users on par.

sections.label: EV adoption under Green Plan
sections.summary: The passage states that as part of the Green Plan there is a strong push to encourage EV adoption, and that 11.8% of new vehicles registered in 2022 were EVs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As part of the Green Plan, there is a strong push to encourage adoption of electric vehicles (EVs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: We understand that 11.8% of all the new vehicles registered last year, in 2022, were EVs.

sections.label: Bus service 137 in Kaki Bukit
sections.summary: The passage states that bus service 137, launched in October 2017 with Downtown Line stage 3, is the newest and only trunk bus service available to Kaki Bukit ward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The newest and only trunk bus service that was made available to Kaki Bukit ward is bus service 137, launched in October 2017, in tandem with the opening of the Downtown Line, stage 3.

sections.label: Public transport fare subsidies
sections.summary: The Government gave about $200 million extra subsidy in 2023, keeping the fare increase at 2.9% for the 2022 fare review exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In October last year, the Government announced that it will provide an additional subsidy of about $200 million in 2023, and this is on top of the current subsidies of more than $2 billion annually to run bus and train services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, the fare increase was kept at 2.9% for the 2022 fare review exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The various support from the Government has enabled the bulk of the fare increases to be deferred and kept our public transport fares affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, the reality is that fare subsidies do come from all the taxes that we all contribute towards – income tax, corporate tax, goods and services tax (GST), plus the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I understand that the public transport fare formula is due for review in 2023.

sections.label: Driver vocational licence age limit
sections.summary: Drivers asked whether the statutory upper age limit of 75 for TDVL and PDVL holders could be raised to 78.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our drivers have asked if it would be possible for a later statutory upper age limit for Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence (TDVL) and Private Hire Car Driver's Vocational Licence (PDVL) holders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is currently at 75 years' old, and our drivers have asked for this to be stretched to 78 as many still feel they are healthy enough to be driving.

sections.label: Vehicle rental price increases
sections.summary: P2P association leaders gave ground feedback that rentals for some vehicle models jumped as much as 35% over the past year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our P2P association leaders have given the ground feedback that rentals for vehicles have jumped as much as 35% over the past year for some rental models.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE premium rise
sections.summary: Last week's COE tender results saw motorcycle premiums rise to $12,189, nearing the record high $13,189 set in November 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Last week's COE tender results saw motorcycle premiums rose to $12,189, nearing the record high $13,189 set in November 2022.

sections.label: Data on motorcycle COE measures
sections.summary: It asks whether there is enough data to assess if raising the motorcycle COE bid deposit to $800 and halving secured COE validity to three months encouraged prudent bidding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Do we have enough data to assess if the measures undertaken last year to raise the bid deposit for motorcycle COEs to $800, from $200 previously and validity of a secured COE will be halved to three months, had made an impact to encourage prudent bidding behaviour?

sections.label: Motorcycle COE measures ineffective
sections.summary: In March last year LTA raised motorcycle COE deposits and halved validity from six to three months, but motorcycle COE still rose to more than $13,000 in November.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In March last year, LTA attempted to arrest high COE prices by increasing the deposit for motorcycles COE and halving their validity period from six months to three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These moves did not arrest the rise in motorcycle COE, which rose to more than $13,000 in November last year.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE open category transfer
sections.summary: The number of motorcycle COEs transferred to the open category was up to 25% before being reduced to 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At one point, the number of motorcycles COE transferred to the open category was up to 25% before being reduced to 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider redesignating some open categories COEs to motorcycle COEs for reasons of equity and fairness for our low-income Singaporeans and of course, the gig economy landscape?

sections.label: Lorry COE expiry
sections.summary: About two-thirds of Singapore's registered lorries, or about 34,000, will have their COEs expire within the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to data from the MOT, about two-thirds of Singapore's registered lorries, or about 34,000, will have their COEs expire within the next five years.

sections.label: Rise in such accidents
sections.summary: The number of such accidents rose to 572 cases in 2020, or 25% more than 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The number of such accidents rose to 572 cases in 2020, or 25% more than 2019.

sections.label: PMD offences on footpaths and roads
sections.summary: 760 persons were caught using PMDs on footpaths in January to November 2022, down from 1,100 in 2021, and 170 were caught riding PMDs on roads, down from 210 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Recently, Minister Iswaran replied to my Parliamentary Question informing that 760 persons were caught using personal mobility devices (PMDs) on footpaths in January to November 2022, down from 1,100 in 2021 and that 170 persons were caught riding PMDs on roads in January to November 2022, as compared to 210 in 2021.

sections.label: Delivery ride laden weight
sections.summary: Currently the laden weight of delivery ride is set at 20 kilograms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Currently the laden weight of delivery ride is set at 20 kilograms.

sections.label: Labour Movement laden weight proposal
sections.summary: The Labour Movement calls for the Ministry to consider allowing a higher laden weight for delivery rides and differentiated laden weights for riders on pathways and roads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: The Labour Movement calls for the Ministry to consider, to allow a higher laden weight for delivery rides and to consider differentiated laden weights, a lighter one for riders who use pathways and a heavier one for riders who are on the roads primarily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Recently, the Active Mobility Advisory Panel proposed a set of rules that would allow for the use of cargo bicycles and other novel mobility devices on our roads and paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While the Panel also recommended that a set of rules on size and weight be consistently applied for these new additions, as with all active mobility devices, many residents are still rightly concerned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Once again, I would like to declare my interest as the President of Strides Mobility Services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: I understand that MOT has conducted at least four sessions of Forward Singapore engagement exercises to gather Singaporeans' view of what they want to see in the future of the Singapore transport system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In these sessions, I understand that many Singaporeans were keen to have a more inclusive transport system that can cater for people with disabilities, the elderly and people with dementia.

sections.label: Public transport and car costs
sections.summary: A speaker is generally happy with public transport but notes younger citizens worry about high COE and ERP costs and road congestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: I used the public transport regularly and other than during peak hours when I experienced more crowdedness on the MRT trains, I am generally quite happy with the state of public transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: However, for some of the younger citizens who aspire towards car ownership, they worry about the high costs of COE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: They also worry about the high ERP charges and ask whether the only solution to road congestion is to impose higher ERP.

sections.label: Road repurposing projects update
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry for an update on road repurposing projects, responses so far, and considerations for rolling them out elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Will the Ministry please give an update to the road repurposing projects announced the responses to these projects thus far and the considerations for road repurposing to be rolled out to other neighbourhoods and communities?

sections.label: Lifts for pedestrian overhead bridges
sections.summary: The passage asks about progress and target timeline for installing lifts on existing pedestrian overhead bridges to provide barrier-free access.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What is the current progress of installing lifts for the existing pedestrian overhead bridges in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What is the target timeline to provide barrier-free access to these bridges, so as to create a more inclusive society, enhancing mobility of seniors, families with young children and those with physical disabilities?

sections.label: Covered linkway at Marsiling
sections.summary: Following appeals, NEA has provided a covered linkway from Marsiling Mall to the overhead bridge and nearby bus stop.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Following our appeals to the relevant agencies, I am heartened that NEA has since provided a covered linkway from the Marsiling Mall to the overhead bridge and nearby bus stop.

sections.label: Inclusive transport and communities
sections.summary: A commuter worried about Orinda in an MRT cabin, and the Enabling Masterplan 2030 lists Inclusive Transport and Inclusive Communities as focal areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Yet, Sophie and Orinda's presence in an MRT cabin last November drew the attention of a concerned fellow commuter, who wondered if she and her child were at risk of being attacked by Orinda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Such incidents aside, the Enabling Masterplan 2030 launched in August last year also featured Inclusive Transport and Inclusive Communities as two of its 14 identified Focal Areas we would need to work on collectively, to become a more disability-inclusive society.

sections.label: Port workers and digitalisation
sections.summary: Unions say a move will affect thousands of port and Tuas workers, and experts rank Singapore among cities best prepared for maritime digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Our unions have told us that this move will affect thousands of workers and this includes not only port workers, but also other workers in the Tuas ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The maritime industry is on the verge of a digital transformation and industry experts have voted Singapore, Oslo, Shanghai and Copenhagen to be the best prepared for the industry digitalisation.

sections.label: digitalPORT@SG and PSA APIs
sections.summary: digitalPORT@SG and PSA's over 50 application programming interfaces let users plug directly into PSA systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The digitalPORT@SG Initiative and PSA's launch of more than 50 application programming interfaces, allows users to plug in directly to PSA systems.

sections.label: Maritime sector cyber security
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government will ensure the maritime sector is prepared for cyber security, noting 200 shipping lines linked to over 600 ports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: How will the Government ensure that the maritime sector is well prepared in the area of cyber security?

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have some 200 shipping lines with links to more than 600 ports in over 120 countries worldwide.

sections.label: Singapore Trade Data Exchange project
sections.summary: SGTraDex aims to give supply chain logistics partners greater visibility, improving asset utilisation, productivity and operational efficiencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One such opportunity is the Singapore Trade Data Exchange (SGTraDex) Project which has the vision to provide greater visibility to supply chain logistics partners, such as haulers and shippers as well as bunkering players, and thereby improve asset utilisation, increase productivity and enhance operational efficiencies.

sections.label: Update on SGTraDex development
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister for an update on SGTraDex's development and other innovative projects anchoring Singapore as industry leader.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share with us an update of the development of SGTraDex and any other innovative projects that will anchor Singapore as the leader in the industry?

sections.label: Changi Airport T5 and traffic recovery
sections.summary: Minister Iswaran said T5 construction resumed on 5 October 2022, expected completion in the mid-2030s, and weekly passenger traffic and flights recovered to about 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Minister Iswaran said on 5 October 2022 that construction work for Changi Airport T5 has resumed after pausing for two years and T5 is expected to be completed in the mid-2030s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: On 9 January 2023, Minister Iswaran also informed the House that the average weekly passenger traffic at Changi Airport has recovered to about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels and the number of weekly flights had also recovered to nearly 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

sections.label: T5 capacity, schedule and runway
sections.summary: The question asks about the option to increase capacity to 70 mppa, the twin phased opening schedule, works status, and whether the new runway can open earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Minister had said in October that we are retaining the option to increase the capacity to up to 70 mppa in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: May the Minister also share with us the likely schedule and dates for the twin phased opening of T5?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: What is the status of these works and when are they scheduled for completion?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: And can the new runway be opened earlier ahead of the projected phased opening of T5?

sections.label: Terminal 5 tender paused
sections.summary: A tender to build T5 was about to be called before the pandemic, but plans were paused for two years due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: As Prime Minister had announced at last year's National Day Rally, we were about to call a tender to build T5 before the pandemic but decided to pause our plans for two years due to COVID-19.

sections.label: Sustainable air hub blueprint
sections.summary: The sustainable air hub blueprint is slated to be unveiled this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Besides the new variables I have already described, the sustainable air hub blueprint is slated to be unveiled this year.

sections.label: Recovery rate and China travel
sections.summary: A question asks whether there is better clarity now on the rate of recovery, especially travel to and from China.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: One, is there better clarity now on the rate of recovery, especially the flow of travels to and from China?

sections.label: Update on Terminal 5 plans
sections.summary: A question asks whether MOT can provide an update on plans for the new Changi Airport Terminal 5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Can MOT provide an update on the plans for the new Changi Airport Terminal 5?

sections.label: Kuala Lumpur-Singapore HSR benefits
sections.summary: The Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail project was expected to bring travel convenience and economic benefits to both countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: The Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail (HSR) project was expected to bring travel convenience and economic benefits to both Singapore and Malaysia.

sections.label: Changi traffic recovery levels
sections.summary: Changi's passenger traffic, flights and city links are at about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels, with a return to pre-pandemic levels expected by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Today, Changi's passenger traffic volumes, flights and city links stand at about 80% of pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Based on the current trajectory, Changi should return to pre-pandemic levels by 2024, possibly earlier.

sections.label: Container throughput and transshipment hub
sections.summary: In 2022, Singapore achieved its second highest container throughput of 37.3 million TEUs and remained the world's largest transshipment hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In 2022, we achieved our second highest container throughput of 37.3 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) and remained the world's largest transshipment hub.

sections.label: Rail network expansion
sections.summary: Ground-breaking ceremonies began for the Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line, with plans to expand the rail network by 100 kilometres over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In January, we held ground-breaking ceremonies to commence work on the Jurong Region Line and the Cross Island Line.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We are on course to expand our rail network by a further 100 kilometres over the next decade, with eight in 10 homes within a 10-minute walk of train stations.

sections.label: Terminal 5 design update
sections.summary: Consultants are updating the design to be more modular, resilient and energy efficient, with T5 planned to be operational in the mid-2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We are working with the consultants to incorporate lessons from the pandemic and update the design to be more modular, resilient and energy efficient.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We plan for T5 to be operational in the mid-2030s.

sections.label: Changi and Tuas port development
sections.summary: The Government will inject $2 billion into the Changi Airport Development Fund, and Tuas Port will be completed in four phases by the 2040s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Government will inject a further $2 billion into the Changi Airport Development Fund (CADF).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Ms Janet Ang asked about the development of Tuas Port, which will be completed in four phases by the 2040s, with an annual handling capacity of 65 million TEUs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Reclamation for Phase 1 has been completed and Phase 2 is at about 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: When the berths in both phases are fully operational, Tuas Port's annual handling capacity will be more than 40 million TEUs.

sections.label: Electric public bus tender
sections.summary: This month, LTA will launch a tender for about 400 electric buses to replace diesel buses reaching end-of-life from December 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about the electrification of our public buses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This month, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) will launch a tender for about 400 electric buses, to replace diesel buses reaching end-of-life from December 2024.

sections.label: Electric airside and heavy vehicles
sections.summary: All new airside light vehicles must be electric from 2025, and certain new heavy vehicles with viable electric models must also be electric from 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: First, all new airside light vehicles, such as cars, vans and minibuses, must be electric from 2025, as they already have viable electric alternatives, which can progressively replace existing diesel models.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We will also require certain new heavy vehicles, like forklifts and tractors, for which viable electric models are available, to be electric from 2025.

sections.label: Harbour craft net-zero emissions
sections.summary: Harbour craft must reach net-zero emissions by 2050, and from 2030 new craft must be fully electric, use B100 biofuels or be net-zero fuel compatible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Moving to the maritime sector, the harbour craft sector will be required to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To achieve this transition, from 2030, all new harbour craft operating in our port waters must be fully electric, be capable of using B100 biofuels or be compatible with net-zero fuels, such as hydrogen.

sections.label: Aviation Sustainability Programme funding
sections.summary: The Government will set up a $50 million Aviation Sustainability Programme to support feasibility trials, research studies and stakeholder collaboration for a sustainable air hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Government will establish a $50 million Aviation Sustainability Programme to support feasibility trials and research studies and bring stakeholders together to create innovative solutions for a more sustainable air hub.

sections.label: Forfeited TCOEs reinjected into Cat D
sections.summary: The forfeited 450 TCOEs will be reinjected into the May to July quarter's Cat D supply, with the market monitored and further moves possible if warranted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The forfeited 450 TCOEs will be reinjected into the May to July quarter's Cat D supply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: I trust that motorcycle buyers and dealers will take this into account when making their decisions to bid or buy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: And we will monitor the market closely and will make further moves if warranted, including a further reduction in the TCOE validity period or a further increase in the bid deposit, as Mr Saktiandi and Mr Singh have suggested.

sections.label: Public transport operating cost subsidies
sections.summary: Public transport operating costs rose about 7% yearly over the last decade while fares rose about 1% yearly, so Government subsidises operating costs over $2 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, operating costs for public transport increased by about 7% per year on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As Members would be aware, fares have gone up by an average of about 1% a year over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Hence, Government subsidises public transport operating costs by more than $2 billion annually and that is about slightly more than $1 per journey.

sections.label: Council review recommendations timing
sections.summary: The council will announce its recommendations by the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To Mr Lim Biow Chuan's query on the progress of this review, the council will announce its recommendations by the second quarter of this year.

sections.label: Cargo bicycle panel recommendations accepted
sections.summary: The Government accepts the Active Mobility Advisory Panel's recommendations on rules and guidelines for cargo bicycles, tricycles and recumbents, to expand transport choices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Fourth, we will also look at ways to expand the range of choices in the transport system, to meet needs that may currently be underserved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: And in this regard, I am happy to share that the Government accepts the Active Mobility Advisory Panel's recommendations on the rules and guidelines for cargo bicycles, tricycles and recumbents.

sections.label: Bus service 137A morning peak
sections.summary: LTA introduced service 137A in 2019, reducing morning peak headway from 15 minutes to a maximum of 10 minutes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: On bus services 137 and 137A, LTA introduced service 137A in 2019 to provide more trips during the morning peak.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This reduced the headway from 15 minutes, which is within Bus Contracting Model standards, to a maximum of 10 minutes during the morning peak.

sections.label: Service 137 loading and trip cuts
sections.summary: In January 2023, Service 137 loading was 58%, but manpower shortages caused two 137A trips to be cut on a few days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In January 2023, the average heaviest one-hour loading for Service 137 at the bus stops before the Bedok North station was 58%, which is within acceptable levels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: However, on a few days in January 2023, the operator reduced two trips for Service 137A due to manpower shortages and this resulted in the higher loading levels which Mr Faisal described.

sections.label: 5G coverage in port areas
sections.summary: Full 5G coverage in anchorages, fairways, terminals and boarding grounds is on track by mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked for an update on our digitalisation plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are on track to provide full 5G coverage in our anchorages, fairways, terminals and boarding grounds by mid-2025.

sections.label: Pilot data reconciliation savings
sections.summary: The pilot reduces manual data reconciliation and can save the industry over S$20 million annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The pilot reduces manual data reconciliation and can save the industry over S$20 million annually.

sections.label: New harbour craft fuel requirements
sections.summary: From 2030, new harbour craft in port waters must be fully electric, use B100 biofuels, or be net-zero fuel compatible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: From 2030, new harbour craft operating in our port waters must be fully electric, be capable of using B100 biofuels, or be compatible with net-zero fuels, such as hydrogen.

sections.label: Land transshipment permit review
sections.summary: The review uses transshipment permits to streamline land transshipment, with potential industry savings of S$2 million annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The review streamlines land transshipment procedures through the use of transshipment permits, similar to existing practices for air and sea transshipment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This will reduce the number of permits that companies need to apply for, with potential cost savings of up to S$40 for each transshipment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The total savings for the industry could amount to S$2 million annually.

sections.label: Allied Container Services Malaysia transport
sections.summary: Allied Container Services can now transport customers' goods directly from Malaysia to Singapore container terminals without double handling.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Allied Container Services will now be able to directly transport the goods of its customers from Malaysia to the container terminals in Singapore, without double handling.

sections.label: Transhipment and export procedures review
sections.summary: Transhipment procedures at land checkpoints are being reviewed and export requirements at the air checkpoint simplified.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: First, we are reviewing our transhipment procedures at the land checkpoints to reduce the number of permits companies need to apply for and help businesses save costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Second, we are simplifying the requirements for exports at our air checkpoint to reduce the level of screening required for goods from companies with strict safety and security processes in place.

sections.label: Foreign drivers accessing container terminals
sections.summary: PSA is working with the industry to let non-Singapore-registered and non-Singaporean drivers under local logistics and haulier companies access container terminals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: PSA is working with the industry to allow non-Singapore-registered and non-Singaporean drivers under local logistics and haulier companies to access the container terminals.

sections.label: App job allocation empty trips
sections.summary: Dynamic job allocation and job pooling provided by the app will reduce empty trips by up to 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: With dynamic job allocation and job pooling provided by the app, the number of empty trips will be reduced by up to 50%.

sections.label: SailMAP Class 1 CoC payment
sections.summary: Under SailMAP, she received $5,000 for attaining her Class 1 Certificate of Competency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Under SailMAP, she received $5,000 for attaining her Class 1 Certificate of Competency (CoC).

sections.label: Silver Zones senior pedestrian accidents
sections.summary: 27 Silver Zones have been implemented, on track for 50 by 2025, with senior pedestrian accident rate reduced by 80%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin will be glad to know that we have implemented 27 Silver Zones so far, and are on track to complete 50 by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Overall, the accident rate for senior pedestrians across all Silver Zones has reduced by 80%.

sections.label: Retrofitting POBs with lifts
sections.summary: 77 POBs have been retrofitted with lifts since 2013, 30 more are continuing, and a new phase will retrofit over 110 more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As Ms Hany Soh highlighted, we have been retrofitting existing POBs with lifts since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: So far, we have completed retrofitting 77 POBs with lifts and will continue with 30 more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As our population ages, the need for more POBs to be retrofitted with lifts will grow.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We are, thus, looking to launch a new phase to retrofit over 110 more existing POBs with lifts.

sections.label: Launching Friendly Streets initiative
sections.summary: The Friendly Streets initiative is launched to harness streets to connect people, activate spaces and strengthen local identity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: More importantly, over time, they impact the way Singaporeans interact with each other – taking care of more vulnerable users, being more gracious to one another.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This is why we are launching the Friendly Streets initiative – to harness the potential of our streets to connect people, activate spaces and strengthen the sense of local identity.

sections.label: Friendly Streets features and pilot locations
sections.summary: Friendly Streets will add pedestrian crossings and cut waiting times, with committees in each locality and pilots in five locations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Second, by facilitating more direct and safer journeys to amenities and transport nodes by implementing more pedestrian crossings where there are natural pedestrian flows and reducing pedestrians' waiting time to cross the road.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: While there will be some common features for Friendly Streets, we hope to have designs unique to each area, co-created with the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will form a Friendly Streets Committee in each locality to spearhead this effort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For a start, we will pilot the Friendly Streets initiative around some streets in five locations – Ang Mo Kio, Bukit Batok West, Tampines, Toa Payoh and West Coast.

sections.label: Friendly Streets pilot timeline
sections.summary: Engagements for Friendly Streets in the five locations start this year, with pilots targeted to be realised by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Engagements for Friendly Streets in these five locations will start this year, with the pilots targeted to be realised by 2025.

sections.label: Islandwide charging points count
sections.summary: There are over 3,800 charging points islandwide today, up from 1,500 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To Prof Koh Lian Pin's question, there are over 3,800 charging points islandwide today, up from 1,500 in 2019.

sections.label: EV Common Charger Grant extension
sections.summary: LTA has co-funded 267 chargers in 107 condominiums, and the EV Common Charger Grant will be extended to December 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To date, LTA has co-funded 267 chargers in 107 condominiums.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we will extend the EV Common Charger Grant for another two years to December 2025.

sections.label: EV charging points tender
sections.summary: LTA launched a large-scale tender last year to deploy 12,000 more EV charging points at around 2,000 HDB carparks in the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Building on this experience, LTA launched a large-scale tender last year to deploy 12,000 more EV charging points at around 2,000 HDB carparks in the next three years.

sections.label: Electric LGV registrations share
sections.summary: Last year, electric LGVs accounted for over 30% of new LGV registrations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Last year, electric LGVs, or e-LGVs accounted for over 30% of new LGV registrations.

sections.label: P2P and taxi driver decline
sections.summary: Monthly active P2P drivers dropped from around 69,000 pre-COVID-19 to 55,000 in the fourth quarter of 2022, with around 9,000 fewer active taxi drivers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The number of monthly active P2P drivers dropped from around 69,000 pre-COVID-19, to 55,000 in the fourth quarter of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The decline is steeper for taxi drivers as there are around 9,000 fewer active drivers, compared to pre-COVID-19, and many who left were two-shift drivers who would drive night or weekend shifts.

sections.label: P2P vocational licence applications
sections.summary: P2P vocational licence applications increased in the past year, with 950 new applications per month in 2022, up from about 650 per month in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we have seen an increase in P2P vocational licence applications in the past year, with 950 new applications per month in 2022, up from about 650 per month in 2021.

sections.label: Shared cars and car sharing
sections.summary: With over 5,000 shared cars in Singapore today, operators plan to expand fleets, and LTA will further study car sharing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With over 5,000 shared cars throughout Singapore today, operators plan to expand their fleets further to meet expected demand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As car sharing can add to our mix of connectivity options for occasional car users, LTA will be further studying car sharing.

sections.label: Registered device passes count
sections.summary: As at end-2022, there are 39,000 passes, an increase of 8,000 from the previous year, accounting for almost 93% of the existing registered device population.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As at end-2022, we have 39,000 passes, which is an increase of 8,000 from the previous year and accounts for almost 93% of the existing registered device population.

sections.label: AM accidents and fires drop
sections.summary: AM-related accidents on public paths and fires involving motorised AM devices each fell by more than 30% since 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The number of AM-related accidents on public paths and fire incidents have dropped significantly, each by more than 30% since 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The number of accidents on paths fell from 155 to 101, while the number of fires involving motorised AM devices fell from 63 in 2021 to 42 in 2022.

sections.label: AM device size limits
sections.summary: A width limit of 1.3 metres and length limit of 2.6 metres will be introduced on all AM devices used on roads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This is to address concerns that overly wide or long devices are less manoeuvrable and may pose safety risks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will introduce a width limit of 1.3 metres and length limit of 2.6 metres on all AM devices used on roads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: These limits are pegged to the largest AM devices being used in Singapore today: 1.3 metres is about the width limit of a trishaw, while 2.6 metres is the length of a two-seater tandem bicycle.

sections.label: Review of PMA regulations
sections.summary: The regulations of PMAs will be reviewed to ensure public safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To ensure public safety, we will review the regulations of PMAs.

sections.label: Total cycling path length
sections.summary: With about 30 kilometres of cycling paths launched recently in various towns, Singapore now has about 550 kilometres of cycling paths in total.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: With the launch of about 30 kilometres of cycling paths in various towns across Singapore recently, we now have about 550 kilometres of cycling paths in total.

sections.label: Cycling paths in HDB towns
sections.summary: All 27 HDB towns and estates can look forward to having some cycling paths by the end of next year, up from the current 13.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: With this, all 27 HDB towns and estates can look forward to having some cycling paths by the end of next year, up from the current 13.

sections.label: On-road cycling lane hours
sections.summary: A 4.6-kilometre on-road cycling lane was demarcated and set aside for buses and cyclists only, on Sundays from 5.00 am to 11.00 am.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: A 4.6-kilometre on-road cycling lane was demarcated and set aside for buses and cyclists only, on Sundays from 5.00 am to 11.00 am.

sections.label: Dementia Go-To Points designation
sections.summary: All MRT stations, bus interchanges and Integrated Transport Hubs have been designated as Dementia Go-To Points.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: First, I am happy to share that all MRT stations, bus interchanges and Integrated Transport Hubs have been designated as Dementia Go-To Points.

sections.label: Covered linkway network expansion
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2022, the covered linkway network was expanded by about 72 kilometres, reaching 275 kilometres built by LTA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Over 2019 to 2022, we expanded our network of covered linkways by about 72 kilometres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Today, we have a total of 275 kilometres of covered linkways built by LTA.

sections.label: Caring Commuter Champion training
sections.summary: In 2022, more than 900 people were trained to assist commuters in need under the Caring Commuter Champion initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In 2022, we had a new initiative to spread awareness to more people.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: I am glad to share that more than 900 people have undergone training to assist commuters in need under the Caring Commuter Champion initiative.

sections.label: Expanding Caring Commuter Champions
sections.summary: The Caring Commuter Champion initiative will expand, with content for primary school children being developed this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Mr Eric Chua may be glad to learn that we will expand the Caring Commuter Champion initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This year, we are developing content that is suitable for primary school children to enlarge our pool of young Caring Commuter Champions.

sections.label: Helping Hand scheme expansion
sections.summary: From April 2023, the Helping Hand scheme will be expanded by adding more messages to assist other commuters' special needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: From April 2023 onwards, we will expand the Helping Hand scheme by adding more messages to assist the special needs of other commuters.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE financing questions
sections.summary: Questions were raised on monitoring repossessed motorcycles, alternative financing options, motorcycle COEs transferred to the Open Category, and increasing motorcycle COEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of high motorcycles COE prices, does MOT, for example, monitor the number of repossessed motorcycles and would it consider doing so to have a better fix on the impact of motorcycle financing through dealerships today?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, would the Ministry consider a broader study into alternative financing options for our motorcycle riders, such as through cooperatives, that could bargain for not just better block-financing rates from financial institutions, but also reduce the arbitrage component of some loans that are, in turn, offered by some motorcycle finance companies today?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the Minister have a perspective on the total number of motorcycle COEs transferred to the Open Category over the last 10 years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider an increase in motorcycle COEs to make up for the COEs transferred to the Open Category in the past?

sections.label: Zero vehicle growth rate
sections.summary: The vehicle growth rate will be zero, making any COE re-allocation a zero-sum exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, I start with the vehicle growth rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We have taken an important, albeit difficult decision, that the vehicle growth rate will be zero.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, that is the first and important consideration, the baseline point: that vehicle growth rate is zero.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is important because the moment we agree on that – and I am assuming the Leader of the Opposition agrees with that as a principle – then any mechanism to re-allocate COEs is basically a zero-sum exercise.

sections.label: Forfeited TCOEs re-enter supply
sections.summary: 450 TCOEs were forfeited in recent months after market pushback, and these re-enter the supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I have pointed out, the most recent couple of months have been quite telling because there have been 450 TCOEs that have been forfeited.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Which means at a certain point, there was pushback in the market and now the dealers have had to let the TCOEs go; and these re-enter the supply.

sections.label: Investigating Hire Purchase Act contraventions
sections.summary: Practices contravening Hire Purchase Act regulations will be investigated thoroughly as they affect the COE market.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: What we will do, however, is that even though the Hire Purchase Act is under MTI, if there are issues about practices that contravene the regulations, these are areas that we will want to make sure they are investigated thoroughly, because they do affect the effective functioning of the COE market.

sections.label: Motorcycle population and Cat E allocation
sections.summary: Singapore's motorcycle population has been around 130,000 to 140,000 over the last 10 years, with Cat E receiving allocations from other categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, the population of motorcycles in Singapore has been around 130,000 to 140,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, it has been at about that level.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And when we talk about allocation to Cat E, it is not just from Cat D.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And we continue to have allocation from Cat A, Cat B and Cat C into Cat E, which then gets recycled.

sections.label: System worked but prices rose
sections.summary: The system has generally worked, but it is being discussed today because prices have gone up.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Because it is a system that, in general, has worked.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But let us also be clear: why we are discussing this today is because the prices have gone up.

sections.label: Arbitrage possibility in market
sections.summary: If arbitrage exists and the market functions well, someone would take advantage and enter.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As the Leader of the Opposition said, if there is an arbitrage possibility and if the market is functioning well, then somebody would take advantage of the arbitrage and come in – whether it is a cooperative or another finance business or whatever.

sections.label: 60,000 electric vehicles by 2030
sections.summary: The estimate is that 60,000 vehicles by 2030 should serve at least half the car population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As we have said, 60,000 by 2030, our estimate is that they should be able to serve at least half the car population.

sections.label: West Camp Road time-based lane
sections.summary: A first time-based lane at West Camp Road is open to cyclists and buses only for six hours a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Therefore, we came up with this first time ever time-based lane at West Camp Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: So, for six hours a week, it is open to cyclists and buses only.

sections.label: Seletar cycling lane permanence
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the cycling lane at Seletar will become permanent if all things go well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: If all things go well, I hope the cycling lane at Seletar will become a permanent one.

sections.label: Electric replacement fleet
sections.summary: As the existing fleet reaches end of life, the replacement has to be electric, with life cycle cost evening out.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As the existing fleet reaches its end of life, the replacement has to be electric.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Even today, based on our discussions with the operators like the larger players, the life cycle cost evens out when you make the switch.

sections.label: Friendly Streets in Toa Payoh
sections.summary: The speaker lauds Friendly Streets and is happy it will be launched in Toa Payoh as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My first question is with regard to the Friendly Streets, which I laud, and I am happy to hear that Friendly Streets will be launched in Toa Payoh as well.

sections.label: 400 new electric buses
sections.summary: The Minister mentioned 400 new electric buses and electrification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Minister mentioned 400 new electric buses and electrification.

sections.label: Affordable electric motorbike trials
sections.summary: Various trials are being run on affordable electric motorbikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: On affordable electric motorbikes, we are running various trials, as Mr Saktiandi would be aware.

sections.label: Battery fire safety concerns
sections.summary: Concerns centre on fire safety, including charging arrangements for removable batteries.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our concerns would, in particular, centre on fire safety type issues, because if they are batteries that can be removed, then, what is the charging arrangement and so on?

sections.label: Speeding up electric buses
sections.summary: The passage asks whether buses and electric buses can be sped up.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: On buses and electric buses, can we speed it up?

sections.label: Non-compliant PAB offences
sections.summary: Non-compliant PAB offences have come down since 2020, with about 600 summonses last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Dennis Tan that, indeed, when we restricted the usage of PMDs, more will then use PABs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But looking at the data that we have, on the offences where we have caught people using non-compliant PABs, they have come down since 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Last year, we had about 600 summonses given for non-compliant PABs.

sections.label: Chargers tapping the grid
sections.summary: The practical way forward is for chargers to tap off the grid rather than dedicated solar panels.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Just on the specific point that Mr Dennis Tan raised, I think the practical way forward is for our chargers to tap off the grid rather than have dedicated solar panels or other sources of energy coming in.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Then, you need batteries to store the electricity in order to do this.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, the more efficient way of doing this is to have the diversification and the incorporation of renewable energies at the grid level – which is what the EMA is doing by calling for proposals for renewable energy supply into Singapore.
